questions.question: You are running late for a meeting. A colleague says to you: 'I thought you were coming earlier.' How could you respond appropriately?
options: I'm so sorry, I got stuck in traffic.
I hope you don't mind, I'll be there soon.
No, I wasn't planning to come early.
Actually, I didn't know the meeting was on.
questions.answer: I'm so sorry, I got stuck in traffic.

questions.question: A friend invites you to a party but you cannot attend. Which response would be most appropriate?
options: I can't, I have to work.
Sorry, I wish I could, but I'm busy that night.
No, I don't want to go.
I don't know, maybe another time.
questions.answer: Sorry, I wish I could, but I'm busy that night.

questions.question: A classmate suggests you borrow their laptop. Which is the best way to politely agree?
options: I don't think so.
No way, I can't borrow that.
Okay, thanks for offering.
I wouldn't dream of it.

questions.question: Your teacher asks for your opinion on a new school policy. Which response best expresses your view clearly?
options: I don't know what to think.
I think it's a good idea, but maybe we could improve it.
I disagree completely.
It doesn't matter to me.
questions.answer: I think it's a good idea, but maybe we could improve it.

questions.question: You are in a formal meeting and someone proposes an idea. Which response shows polite disagreement?
options: I'm not sure I agree with that.
That's not right at all.
I think you're mistaken.
No, I don't think so.
questions.answer: I'm not sure I agree with that.
